formula: post_test ~ treatment + pre_test + treatment:pre_test + grade + (1 | pair_id)
notes: ROS ElectricCompany example (electric.R) fits classical stan_glm(post_test ~ treatment + pre_test + treatment:pre_test) within each grade; no multilevel fit in the book. 96 matched class pairs (pair_id, 2 rows each: treated + control) nested in 4 grades; rendered (1 | pair_id) per Tier T rule. X row id and supp (secondary supplement treatment, NA for controls) ignored. Read electric.R and the electric codebook.

ROS Helicopters data-collection exercise; no model fitted in the book. Repeated flight times per paper helicopter: Helicopter_ID repeats (several time_sec per helicopter, width/length constant within helicopter). Rendered as repeated-measures (1 | Helicopter_ID). Read the helicopters codebook.

ROS Earnings example (earnings_regression.R) fits classical stan_glm(earn ~ height + male); no multilevel fit in the book. ethnicity (White/Black/Hispanic/Other) is carried in the table; ARM Ch.13 (Gelman & Hill 2007, stan_arm earnings_vary_si) fits a varying intercept/slope by ethnicity, so ethnicity is rendered as the grouping cluster. earn is log-modelled; earnk (earn in $1000s) is the duplicate response, ignored. RULE GAP: ethnicity is a 4-level demographic, treated as a grouping here only because a published ARM model groups on it; a handful-level demographic is otherwise a covariate.

formula: partyid7 ~ real_ideo + race_adj + age_discrete + educ1 + female + income + (1 | year)
notes: ROS NES example (nes_linear.R) fits classical stan_glm(partyid7 ~ real_ideo + race_adj + factor(age_discrete) + educ1 + female + income) separately within each election year; no pooling/multilevel in the book. year repeats across respondents (1952-2000 election waves); rendered (1 | year) per Tier T 'year in election tables' rule. partyid7 is a 7-point party-ID scale (ordinal). age_discrete wrapped in factor(); resid row id and survey weights weight1-3 ignored. Read nes_linear.R.

ROS NES logistic example (nes_logistic.R) fits classical stan_glm(rvote ~ income, binomial) within one election year (1992); no multilevel in the book. Second documented model (binary Republican-vote response, differs from the partyid7 model); rendered (1 | year). Read nes_logistic.R.

ROS Pew example (pew.R) describes party identification by income/ideology and summarises by state (as.numeric(pew_pre$state)); it fits no multilevel model. Respondents nested in state (50 + DC), the sampling cluster of this election survey; rendered (1 | state) per Tier T 'state in election tables' rule. Response party (republican/democrat/independent/no-preference/other, filed categorical); income and ideo are ordered Stata factors. rid respondent id and survey weight ignored. RULE GAP: the response is inferred (the book is descriptive, no fitted outcome model). Read pew.R and the Stata codebook.

ROS Storable-votes example (storable.R, ROS Ch.15) fits classical stan_polr(factor_vote ~ value) separately per subject (person); ordered 3-level vote (1/2/3). person repeats across rounds (repeated measures); rendered (1 | person). cutoff.12, cutoff.23, sd.logit are fitted per-person parameters (derived), ignored; school is the session, round/proposal design indices. Two-player-game sessions. Read storable.R.

ROS Storable-votes example (storable.R, ROS Ch.15) fits classical stan_polr(factor_vote ~ value) per subject (person); ordered 3-level vote. person repeats across rounds; rendered (1 | person). cutoff.12/cutoff.23/sd.logit are fitted per-person parameters (derived), ignored; school the session, round/proposal design indices. Three-player-game sessions. Read storable.R.

ROS Storable-votes example (storable.R, ROS Ch.15) fits classical stan_polr(factor_vote ~ value) per subject (person); ordered 3-level vote. person repeats across rounds; rendered (1 | person). cutoff.12/cutoff.23/sd.logit are fitted per-person parameters (derived), ignored; school the session, round/proposal design indices. Six-player-game sessions. Read storable.R.

ROS Sesame IV example (sesame.R) fits classical stan_glm using as.factor(site) as a FIXED factor: postlet ~ watched_hat + prelet + factor(site) + setting; no multilevel. 240 children nested in 5 study sites (sesame_codebook.txt); site rendered as the grouping cluster (1 | site) per Tier T rule. encouraged is the randomised instrument. Alternate pre/post subtests and constructed columns (y dup of postlet, pretest dup of prelet, _Isite dummies, watched/regular alternate codings) ignored; the book models only postlet. Read sesame.R and sesame_codebook.txt.

ROS Sesame IV example (sesame.R) fits classical stan_glm with as.factor(site) FIXED; 240 children in 5 study sites, rendered (1 | site) per Tier T rule. Alternate pre/post subtests and constructed columns ignored; the book models only postlet. Read sesame.R and sesame_codebook.txt.

NYC Housing and Vacancy Survey rodent data (ARM Ch.14 rodents exercise); no model fitted in the ROS repo. Binary rodent2 (rodent presence, per Data Dictionary.txt) over apartments nested in cd (55 community districts), borough the coarser cluster (5). Rendered (1 | cd); race (ethnicity code) the key predictor. The *_Mean columns are community-level group means (derived), sequenceno a row id, housewgt a survey weight, povertyx2 a derived poverty recode, all ignored. RESPONSE INFERRED from the Data Dictionary. apt.dat, hvs02_unsorted and the subsets are duplicates of this study (excluded). Read Data Dictionary.txt.

ROS Childcare example (childcare.R) uses the IHDP data for propensity-score matching with stan_glm; it fits no multilevel model. Children nested in 8 study states/sites (state; st5..st53 dummies); rendered (1 | state) per Tier T rule. Outcome ppvtr.36 (age-3 vocabulary test), treat the intervention. Many engineered dummies (state/age/education indicators) and transformed columns (bwT, neg.bw, momageT) ignored. RULE GAP: state here is the 8-site study structure, used only as optional propensity covariates rather than a modelled random effect; filed as a repeating cluster per the #24 cluster-that-repeats rule. Read childcare.R.
